## Search Paths

Phase 0 rewrote the question into three declarative sub-queries (science goals / dates + light-curve count / CoRoT-7b bright-star limit). Phase 1 wide net: **`kb_search_vector`** (kb_id=`1e6199ea-f380-44e2-94fc-d431f0f9bb6b`, top_k=30, score_threshold=0.35, balance_kbs=True) ran all three → 90 raw hits → doc-level dedup → **3 candidate documents kept (no top-N cut)**. Verify input: **`kb_doc_read`** on every candidate (the CoRoT paper read end-to-end, 151 lines). Recall was triply corroborated by `kb_search` metadata scan (1 hit) and `kb_search_two_stage` BM25+graph (CoRoT doc ranked #1, stage1=21.48, ~1.8× runner-up). **The Laya `jev_filter` engine gate could not be executed in the subagent's session** (no shell tool; no MCP-tool equivalent for Laya scoring) — this is reported honestly below rather than papered over.

## Answer

All four parts are answered verbatim by a single document, *The CoRoT exoplanet program: status & results* (arXiv:1105.1887).

**1. Science goals — two distinct objectives.**
> "CoRoT has been designed with two distinct scientific objectives which both require continuous observations and ultra-high precision relative stellar photometry: one is **the detection of extrasolar planets by the transit method**; the second is **the study of stellar interiors by asteroseismology** (Baglin et al. 2009). In addition, the long duration of the observation periods together with the exquisite photometric precision allow number of stellar physics studies."

**2. Start of science observations and mission extension.**
> "The instrument started the scientific observations on **February 2nd 2007**. The mission was initially scheduled for **3 years but extended for 3 additional years, that is till March 2013**."

**3. Light curves collected by summer 2010.**
> "In **summer 2010, a total of 129 326 light curves was collected** (Table 1)."
Transits are detected in about 100–300 light curves per run (≈3000 for the whole mission to date). After the DPU-1 breakdown of March 2009, the number of light curves per field was halved.

**4. Why CoRoT-7b-type super-Earths are only found around bright stars.**
> "It shows that **Neptune size planets can be detected whatever the magnitude of the star is, whereas super-Earth size planets, such as CoRoT-7b can be discovered in the light curves of stars brighter than R ≈ 14 only**."

The reason is signal-to-noise on a shallow transit: the detection signal is the product of relative transit depth and √(number of in-transit points). CoRoT-7b's transit is only **0.35 mmag deep**, so it is lost in photon noise unless the host star is bright (low noise). CoRoT-7b "orbits in 0.8 days a K0 main sequence star which is one of the brightest star in the first long run in the anti-center direction."
